claim: A group may straddle the seam: four birds at x = 30.5, 31.5, 0.5 and 1.5 are one group.
derivation: Four birds on y = 10 at x = 30.5, 31.5, 0.5 and 1.5, all heading (1, 0), on a 32 × 32 world.
31.5 to 0.5 is −31, which wraps to +1 (E1), so consecutive birds are 1 apart across the seam, with the same heading: one cluster of 4, one group (E14). clusterCount = 1.
All headings agree: directionalAgreement = 1 (E12). Every nearest neighbour is 1 away: meanNeighbourDistance = 1 (E13).
No strays: strayShare = 0 (E18). One group holding every bird reads as one group (O1).

The group spans the seam: x = 30.5, 31.5, 0.5, 1.5 sit symmetrically about 0 the short way round, so the centre is (0, 10). Offsets -1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5, so the mean squared distance is 5/4 and groupSpread = √1.25 (E19). No obstacles: birdsAtObstacles = 0 (E20).
